newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey recalls ambassador to Libya.
newsitem.headline: Turkey recalls ambassador to Libya.

text.p: Turkey has recalled its ambassador to Libya after sharp criticism by Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi of Turkey's month-long incursion into northern Iraq and military cooperation with Israel, a Foreign Ministry statement said on Friday.

"It has been decided that our ambassador in Tripoli...be recalled because of the continuing and recently totally offensive remarks by the Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi about our country and our armed forces," the statement said.
"The Jews who rule the Turkish army made it (take a stand) against the Arabs," Gaddafi said in a speech on Wednesday in the Libyan city of Derna.
Thousands of Turkish troops poured into northern Iraq on May 14 in pursuit of Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas fighting for self-rule in southeastern Turkey.
Most Arab states protested against the incursion, calling for the respect of integrity and unity of Iraqi soil.
Arab countries were also worried about Turkish-Israeli defence deals signed by the two states in the last 18 months.
